revivals.subject: 1920s suit
revivals.quote: At this time, tweed cloth sportcoats became acceptable town wear, and business suits imitated the broad shouldered, form fitting styles of the 1920s, sometimes with contrasting lapel piping.

revivals.subject: 1930s cabaret
revivals.quote: Fashion was based on varied looks inspired by historical Romantic themes, including frilly fop shirts in the style of the English Romantic period, Russian constructivism, Bonnie Prince Charlie, French Incroyables and 1930s' Cabaret, Hollywood starlets, Puritans and the Pierrot clown, with any look being possible if it was adapted to be unusual and striking.

revivals.subject: 1930s hollywood glamour
revivals.quote: Visually, it was a mesh of various styles, ranging from 1930s Hollywood glamour, through 1950s pin-up sex appeal, pre-war cabaret theatrics, Victorian literary and symbolist styles, science fiction, to ancient and occult mysticism and mythology; manifesting itself in outrageous clothes, makeup, hairstyles, and platform-soled boots.

revivals.subject: 1930s to 1960s vintage clothing
revivals.quote: Other women just adopted simple casual fashions, or combined new garments with carefully chosen secondhand or vintage clothing from the 1930s, 1950s and 1960s.

revivals.subject: 1930s-50s haircuts
revivals.quote: In the early 2010s, men's 1930s, 1940s, and 1950s haircuts underwent a revival, with many British professionals aged 18–50 wearing businessman's haircuts with side partings, quiffs or slicked back hair.

revivals.subject: 1940s makeup
revivals.quote: By around 2005/06, retro-styled makeup from the 1940s had made a comeback, such as bright red lips and cat eyes.

revivals.subject: 1940s movie star glamour
revivals.quote: Many women still continued to dress up with more glamorous clothes, inspired by 1940s movie star glamour.

revivals.subject: 1940s style sandals
revivals.quote: For more casual occasions, women opted for lean capri pants, polka dot blouses, belted trench coats, 1940s style sandals, white canvas shoes especially Keds, leggings with oversized tops, slouch socks with leggings, stirrup pants worn over tights or pantyhose with flats and an oversized top, rolled jeans or khakis or shorts or shortalls, shortalls, bell bottoms and wide leg jeans, sweaters, sweatshirts, tunic tops, shorts suit with dress shorts with tights underneath, ballet flats and a top and jacket, above the knee dresses sometimes worn with bike shorts underneath

revivals.subject: 1940s styles
revivals.quote: It has been largely inspired by styles of the late 1970s to late 1980s, the late 1990s to mid-2000s, and elements of Modern Medieval fashion, boho-chic, Indie sleaze and mid-century fashions from the 1940s, 1950s and 1960s.

revivals.subject: 1940s-style hat
revivals.quote: Accessories included scarves, gold jewelry, flowers, ankle boots, 1940s style hats (often tilted), skinny and wide belts, boas, braceleted gloves, spike-heeled sandals, mules, ankle-strapped shoes, waist cinchers, and obi wraps.

revivals.subject: 1950s menswear
revivals.quote: During the late 2000s, men's fashion incorporated styles inspired by the 1950s and 1980s.

revivals.subject: 1950s styles
revivals.quote: Additionally, fashion trends throughout the decade recycled styles from previous decades, most notably the 1950s, 1960s and 1970s.

revivals.subject: 1950s styles
revivals.quote: Fast fashion retailers such as Topshop, Forever 21, and H&M popularized vintage-inspired styles, replicating elements from the 1950s, and 1980s.

revivals.subject: 1950s styles
revivals.quote: It has been largely inspired by styles of the late 1970s to late 1980s, the late 1990s to mid-2000s, and elements of Modern Medieval fashion, boho-chic, Indie sleaze and mid-century fashions from the 1940s, 1950s and 1960s.

revivals.subject: 1950s vintage clothing
revivals.quote: Common items included mini skirts, bell-bottoms popularized by hippies, vintage clothing from the 1950s and earlier, and the androgynous glam rock and disco styles that introduced platform shoes, bright colors, glitter, and satin.

revivals.subject: 1960s and 1970s rock
revivals.quote: Originating in the late 1990s and early 2000s amongst New York City's post-punk revival scene, which encompassed bands like the Strokes, Yeah Yeah Yeahs and Interpol, the style began as a way for bands to visually reference the 1960s and 1970s artists they were musically influenced by.

revivals.subject: 1960s styles
revivals.quote: Additionally, fashion trends throughout the decade recycled styles from previous decades, most notably the 1950s, 1960s and 1970s.

revivals.subject: 1960s styles
revivals.quote: Later in the decade, fashion increasingly incorporated styles inspired by the 1960s, 1970s, and 1980s.

revivals.subject: 1960s styles
revivals.quote: It has been largely inspired by styles of the late 1970s to late 1980s, the late 1990s to mid-2000s, and elements of Modern Medieval fashion, boho-chic, Indie sleaze and mid-century fashions from the 1940s, 1950s and 1960s.

revivals.subject: 1970s and 1980s fashion
revivals.quote: Indie sleaze fashion was characterized by traits of 1970s and 1980s fashion, in addition to grunge fashion, which Daniel Rodgers of Dazed described as "grubby, maximalist, and performatively vintage" and by NME's El Hunt as being defined by a sense of "chaotic spontaneity".

revivals.subject: 1970s and 1980s menswear
revivals.quote: Due to the continued influence of vintage fashion and retro-inspired pop culture, 1970s and 1980s styles maintained a steady presence in the fashion industry throughout the 2020s.

revivals.subject: 1970s fashion
revivals.quote: This was part of a wave of 1970s nostalgia that was taking place in popular culture at the time.

revivals.subject: 1970s fashion
revivals.quote: By 2018, a 1970s revival began to replace the mid-decade's 90s inspired looks, inspired by designers such as Alessandro Michele at Gucci.

revivals.subject: 1970s styles
revivals.quote: Later in the decade, fashion increasingly incorporated styles inspired by the 1960s, 1970s, and 1980s.

revivals.subject: 1980s and 1990s menswear
revivals.quote: In the summer of 2011, 1980s and 1990s inspired fashion made a comeback among men.

revivals.subject: 1980s and early 1990s styles
revivals.quote: During the late 2000s, fashion in Europe and the United States saw another revival of styles from the 1980s and early 1990s.

revivals.subject: 1980s fashion
revivals.quote: The revival of 1980s fashion began in the late 1990s and continued into the early 2000s, with an initial focus on styles from the early part of the decade.Popular clothing included denim miniskirts, "distressed" jeans, denim jackets, tracksuits, trench coats, puffy jackets, and polo shirts with raised collars.

revivals.subject: 1980s styles
revivals.quote: Later in the decade, fashion increasingly incorporated styles inspired by the 1960s, 1970s, and 1980s.

revivals.subject: 1980s styles
revivals.quote: Fast fashion retailers such as Topshop, Forever 21, and H&M popularized vintage-inspired styles, replicating elements from the 1950s, and 1980s.

revivals.subject: 1980s styles
revivals.quote: After the COVID-19 pandemic began, fashion trends shifted significantly, with a resurgence of 1980s-inspired styles such as scrunchies and modern 80s hairstyles.

revivals.subject: 1980s tailoring
revivals.quote: More formal styles intended for the workplace or special occasions (such as a cocktail party) included silk blouses in neutral colors or animal prints, tailored pantsuits and skirt suits inspired by the 1980s, collarless coats, and the little black dress, with or without subtle embroidery.

revivals.subject: 2000s menswear
revivals.quote: During the 2022 FIFA World Cup, Welsh fans brought back various 2000s fashion trends.

revivals.subject: 40s-by-way-of-70s dresses
revivals.quote: Cobain's style was a combination from both male and female fashion, and "his Seattle thrift-store look ran the gamut of masculine lumberjack workwear and 40s-by-way-of-70s feminine dresses."

revivals.subject: art nouveau jewellery
revivals.quote: The Art Nouveau movement of 1890-1910 inspired most of the natural forms and geometric shapes of the jewelry during the 1920s.

revivals.subject: bustle
revivals.quote: Bustled and fuller skirts reflected a 19th-century influence; hats reached extravagant towering heights.

revivals.subject: early 2010s
revivals.quote: The early 2020s trend cycle seemed to contradict itself, with microtrends like the Y2K revival and early 2010s nostalgia emerging alongside the millennial backlash.

revivals.subject: edwardian silhouettes
revivals.quote: Other monochromatic trends during this period included Edwardian-style high-necked blouses and lace maxi-dresses, tuxedo jackets with contrasting velvet or satin lapels, vests, and duster coats reflecting a shift in vintage revivalism from mid-century to early-20th century silhouettes.

revivals.subject: elizabethan ruffled collar
revivals.quote: For evening, spectacular drapey coats were worn to coordinate with evening dresses, often trimmed with fur, while capes in both short and floor-length versions appeared in fabrics ranging from panné velvet to taffeta, and were sometimes finished with dramatic Elizabethan-inspired ruffled collars.

revivals.subject: late 1970s to late 1980s styles
revivals.quote: It has been largely inspired by styles of the late 1970s to late 1980s, the late 1990s to mid-2000s, and elements of Modern Medieval fashion, boho-chic, Indie sleaze and mid-century fashions from the 1940s, 1950s and 1960s.

revivals.subject: late 1990s to mid-2000s styles
revivals.quote: It has been largely inspired by styles of the late 1970s to late 1980s, the late 1990s to mid-2000s, and elements of Modern Medieval fashion, boho-chic, Indie sleaze and mid-century fashions from the 1940s, 1950s and 1960s.

revivals.subject: mid and late 1990s styles
revivals.quote: Many trends from the mid and late 1990s continued into the early 2000s.

revivals.subject: mid-century modern
revivals.quote: The "mid-century modern" inspired formal wear trend of fall 2025 featured black, navy blue, dark grey and ecru double breasted wool sport coats, and baggy, high waisted pants inspired by Dior's 1954 menswear collection.

revivals.subject: mid-century silhouettes
revivals.quote: Throughout the decade, retro revivals persisted, including 1980s-style neon streetwear and tailored or fit-and-flare mid-century silhouettes that reflected the growing interest in vintage fashion.

revivals.subject: mid-late 1960s secondhand clothing
revivals.quote: Garage punk bands of the 1970s like MC5, Iggy and the Stooges, the Flamin' Groovies and the Ramones often wore secondhand clothing from the mid-late 1960s, such as velvet jackets, slim-fitting grey suits, black leather jackets, winklepickers and drainpipe jeans, in reaction to the flared trousers worn by hippies and disco fans.

revivals.subject: millinery flowers and feathers
revivals.quote: The 1930s saw the return of trimmings such as flowers and feathers in millinery after their near-disappearance in the second half of the 1920s.

revivals.subject: neo-victorian
revivals.quote: From 2011 to 2015, members of this subculture often combined Neo-Victorian and Elegant Gothic aristocrat clothing such as top hats, pocket watches, or (for girls) corsets, velvet or brocade dresses, brooches, and black, dark red or brown leather waistcoats, with bowties, hipster inspired beards and tweed clothing, jewelry made from brass gears, dark skinny jeans, worker boots, and flying goggles.

revivals.subject: redingote
revivals.quote: Evening coats were fabricated in satin, taffeta, moiré faille, and shantung; designers also revived the redingote of the 18th and 19th centuries—formfitting with a nipped-in waist and a long flared skirt—updated for the times.

revivals.subject: regency tailcoat
revivals.quote: Men often wore dramatic cosmetics and androgynous clothing, including ruffled poet shirts, red or blue hussar jackets with gold braid, silk sashes, tight pants, shiny rayon waistcoats, and tailcoats based on those worn during the Regency era.

revivals.subject: retro movie styles
revivals.quote: Movies such Top Gun, Bullitt, and Midnight Cowboy contributed to the popularity of several styles.

revivals.subject: romantic evening gown
revivals.quote: Large volumes of fabric were used to create the fuller silhouette, with long dramatic gowns evoking the 19th century through silk brocade, warp-printed taffeta, ciselé velvet, and elaborate embroidery and beading.

revivals.subject: romantic period dress
revivals.quote: Influenced by David Bowie, Marc Bolan and Roxy Music, the New Romantics developed fashions inspired by the glam rock era coupled with the early Romantic period of the late 18th and early 19th century (from which the movement took its name).

revivals.subject: structured strapless bodice
revivals.quote: This revival of 1940s and '50s styles included the heavily structured and shaped strapless tops seen in bodices of the forties and fifties, achieved with boning and other forms of stiffening.

revivals.subject: victorian and edwardian dandy
revivals.quote: By 1968, the space age mod fashions had been gradually replaced by Victorian, Edwardian and Belle Époque influenced style, with men wearing double-breasted suits of crushed velvet or striped patterns, brocade waistcoats and shirts with frilled collars.

revivals.subject: victorian romanticism
revivals.quote: Other styles that characterized the decade were romanticism, which recovered elements of Victorian fashion; and surrealism, epitomized in the work of designer Elsa Schiaparelli.

revivals.subject: victorian silhouette
revivals.quote: Prairie clothing, pioneer clothing, homesteader clothing, Victorian silhouettes, wool, calico muslin, button downs, and worn leather are often incorporated into the cottagecore style.

revivals.subject: victorian, edwardian and belle époque dress
revivals.quote: Styles of dress within the subculture draw on glam rock, punk, new wave, new romantics and from the fashion of earlier periods such as the Victorian, Edwardian, and Belle Époque eras.

revivals.subject: winterhalter gown
revivals.quote: Reflecting on the romantic fashion of the 1930s, Cecil Willett Cunnington wrote in 1952: "Never has Fashion been more ironic than in this attempt to revive, for an evening dress, the modes current on the eve of the Franco-Prussian War."

revivals.subject: beehive
revivals.quote: Along with these hairstyles, 1960s-inspired beehive hairdos were popularized by British pop singers Emily Capell and Joy Crookes Early 2000s fashion-inspired straightened and brightly dyed hair was made popular by Doja Cat and Billie Eilish from 2021 to 2022.

revivals.subject: bell-bottom jeans
revivals.quote: Bell-bottom jeans from the 1970s were popular again by 1992, along with the baby-doll T-shirt.

revivals.subject: boho
revivals.quote: Drawing loosely from hippie counterculture, the style brought "boho" elements into casual mainstream apparel.

revivals.subject: bouffant
revivals.quote: Meanwhile, most professional men over 30 had conservative 1950s style bouffant haircuts, regular haircuts, or the Caesar cut.

revivals.subject: britpop
revivals.quote: Beginning in March 2017, clothing inspired by 1990s Britpop, mod revival and 1970s fashion became popular among young men in the US, UK, Australia, Canada, Ireland, Italy, Hong Kong, and France, especially in beige, cream, sand, orange, blue, brown, dark green, ecru, red, pistachio, and complementary neutral tones.

revivals.subject: 1990s business casual
revivals.quote: Employees returning to the office frequently combined 1990s fashion–inspired business casual attire with elements of loungewear and athleisure such as monotone sneakers, hoodies, shorts, and dark grey sweatpants.

revivals.subject: pedal pushers and capri pants
revivals.quote: Continuing a trend begun during the late 1970s, cropped pants and revivals of 1950s and early '60s styles like pedal-pushers and Capri pants were popular.

revivals.subject: choker
revivals.quote: 1990s nostalgia appeared in unisex cuts and velvet or lace chokers.

revivals.subject: cigarette holder
revivals.quote: Cigarette holders were revived as sophisticated accessories.

revivals.subject: cloche hat
revivals.quote: Balenciaga had already introduced an unfitted suit jacket in 1951 and showed an unfitted dress by 1954; Dior presented his A line in 1955; and by 1957 the "sack" (or "bag") dress—combining a loose body with a dropped waist that recalled the silhouettes of the 1920s, typically worn with an updated version of the cloche hat—had been launched by multiple designers.

revivals.subject: cocktail dress
revivals.quote: Continuing a trend begun by designers in 1978, the early 1980s also saw a return to pre-sixties ideas of formality, with coordinated suits, occasion dressing like forties-fifties-revival cocktail dresses and evening dresses, and even a revival of hats and gloves, though neither was required for women as they had once been.

revivals.subject: cottagecore
revivals.quote: The aesthetic gained traction in many online spheres and on social media in 2020 due to the mass quarantining in response to the COVID-19 pandemic.

revivals.subject: pump
revivals.quote: In 1979, the higher-vamped, vaguely 1950s-looking pump that would characterize the eighties would appear, often in bright colors and marked by the underslung cone heels introduced by Maud Frizon.

revivals.subject: curtain bangs
revivals.quote: By 2019, curtain bangs began to trend, often paired with layered cuts reminiscent of 90s styles.

revivals.subject: dark academia
revivals.quote: The dark academia or old money aesthetic of the early to mid 2020s, which combined elements of preppy fashion and gothic fashion, was heavily influenced by 1930s and 1940s fashion, particularly attire worn by students at Oxbridge, Ivy League colleges, and prep schools during the time.

revivals.subject: light academia preppy
revivals.quote: A closely related style, known as "light academia", was characterized by neutral and light colors, including soft blues, pinks, whites, creamy yellows, beige, light greys, light purple, pastel and dusty colors, plaid, stripes, and argyle patterns reminiscent of the preppy look of the early 1980s.

revivals.subject: brown lipstick
revivals.quote: By 2015–16, mauve and brown shades of lipstick make a comeback from the 1990s, promoted by Kylie Jenner.

revivals.subject: disco look
revivals.quote: Disco fashion was generally inspired by clothing from the early 1960s.

revivals.subject: disco
revivals.quote: From 1997 onwards, many British and American designers started to take cues from the disco fashion of the mid–late 1970s.

revivals.subject: disco
revivals.quote: In addition to Madonna's disco-influenced attire to award shows and interviews, her Confessions Tour incorporated various elements of the 1970s, such as disco balls, a mirrored stage design, and the roller derby.

revivals.subject: double-breasted suit
revivals.quote: Double breasted suits inspired by the 1940s were reintroduced in the 1980s by designers like Giorgio Armani, Ralph Lauren, and Anne Klein.

revivals.subject: double-breasted blazer
revivals.quote: Double-breasted blazers inspired by 1940s styles returned as power suits in the 1980s.

revivals.subject: dropped waist
revivals.quote: Balenciaga had already introduced an unfitted suit jacket in 1951 and showed an unfitted dress by 1954; Dior presented his A line in 1955; and by 1957 the "sack" (or "bag") dress—combining a loose body with a dropped waist that recalled the silhouettes of the 1920s, typically worn with an updated version of the cloche hat—had been launched by multiple designers.

revivals.subject: brightly dyed hair
revivals.quote: Along with these hairstyles, 1960s-inspired beehive hairdos were popularized by British pop singers Emily Capell and Joy Crookes Early 2000s fashion-inspired straightened and brightly dyed hair was made popular by Doja Cat and Billie Eilish from 2021 to 2022.

revivals.subject: ed hardy
revivals.quote: Brands like Ed Hardy, Hot Topic, and Affliction, which were popular in the late 2000s, made a return, integrating past fashion trends with contemporary preferences.

revivals.subject: emo
revivals.quote: In the early 2020s, alternative fashion drew on past subcultures like emo, pop punk, goth, and scene, as well as Japanese street style and emerging genres like hyperpop, nu metal, shoegaze, and rage music.

revivals.subject: fanny pack
revivals.quote: The fanny pack accessory made a late comeback in 2018 with new packs introduced by fashion designers Gucci, Prada, and Louis Vuitton.

revivals.subject: farrah fawcett hair
revivals.quote: The Farrah Fawcett hairstyle made a comeback, with highlights going hand-in-hand with this revival.

revivals.subject: wings haircut
revivals.quote: In the mid-2000s, longer hair on teenage boys became popular in the UK and America, including the wings haircut, influenced by the 1960s Mod subculture, and British indie pop stars.

revivals.subject: 1920s gatsby
revivals.quote: From 2012 onwards, seersucker blazers and pants made a comeback among young American men due to a resurgence of interest in classic preppy clothing and the 1920s fashion showcased in The Great Gatsby.

revivals.subject: peaky blinders flat cap
revivals.quote: Common accessories included cashmere wool scarfs in neutral tones like white or ecru, loafers, chelsea boots and flat caps inspired by Peaky Blinders.

revivals.subject: fur coat
revivals.quote: Fur coats returned to fashion, while some consumers chose alternative materials in response to concerns about animal cruelty.

revivals.subject: geek chic
revivals.quote: American Apparel made normcore a prominent aspect of hipster culture in the US from 2016 onwards.

revivals.subject: glam rock
revivals.quote: Influenced by David Bowie, Marc Bolan and Roxy Music, the New Romantics developed fashions inspired by the glam rock era coupled with the early Romantic period of the late 18th and early 19th century (from which the movement took its name).

revivals.subject: glam rock
revivals.quote: In addition to the traditional denim and leather look, mainstream heavy metal bands began to dress in more bright, colourful and theatrical clothing similar, in many ways, to the glam rock look of the 1970s.

revivals.subject: dressy hats and gloves
revivals.quote: For fall 1978, designers showed a plethora of mostly small forties- and fifties-looking hats, particularly small, tilted pillboxes, often with veils, and the fashion press claimed that there was an increase in hat sales.

revivals.subject: goth
revivals.quote: This trend would return in the 1990s.

revivals.subject: grandpacore
revivals.quote: The "grandpacore" fashion trend of 2024, also known as "eclectic grandpa", is characterized by vintage-inspired casual fashion from the late 1940s to early 1960s.

revivals.subject: granny boots
revivals.quote: Despite the wide variety, the most popular boots were Go-go boots, crinkle boots (boots with a shiny wet look that was wrinkled), stretch boots, and granny boots (1920s style lace-up boots that ended just below the knees).

revivals.subject: 1990s grunge
revivals.quote: Overarching trends of the decade included hipster fashion, normcore and minimalist aesthetics, and unisex elements inspired by 1990s grunge.

revivals.subject: grunge
revivals.quote: In 2022, Nylon magazine wrote that 1990s Grunge "is one of Fall 2022's biggest fashion trends", with brands and designers such as Marc Jacobs, Molly Goddard, Dsquared2, and Givenchy having collections inspired by grunge fashion.

revivals.subject: grunge
revivals.quote: In June 2025, GQ wrote that grunge style was trending again thanks to TikTok, British singer Charli XCX, and Italian fashion house Magliano's fall-winter 2025 collection inspired by grunge fashion.

revivals.subject: revere collar
revivals.quote: Although shirt collars remained relatively small, by 2019 these began to be replaced in the UK by oversized Revere collars reminiscent of disco fashion.

revivals.subject: forehead headband
revivals.quote: Headbands were worn across the forehead in imitation of 1920s styles, or higher on the crown in reference to 1960s mod fashion.

revivals.subject: mod headband
revivals.quote: Headbands were worn across the forehead in imitation of 1920s styles, or higher on the crown in reference to 1960s mod fashion.

revivals.subject: high top fade
revivals.quote: The High Top Fade, often with a bleached blonde streak inspired by Wiz Khalifa, came back into style among African American youth on the West Coast.

revivals.subject: 1990s hip-hop
revivals.quote: Retro retro 1990s fashions like snapbacks, skinny acid-wash jeans, bucket hats, Retro curved peak mid-late 1990s inspired strapback caps (commonly known as "Dad Hats"), baseball jackets, nylon tracksuits, varsity jackets, Vans, Chuck Taylors, rain boots, retro Nikes, Shell tube socks, leather jackets, Levis, Adidas and Nike apparel, gold chains, Ray Ban sunglasses, Air Jordans, and oversized sweaters, and colors such as red, green, and yellow, made a comeback in the African American community due to the influence of drum and bass, rave music, and indie pop-inspired rappers.

revivals.subject: hippie
revivals.quote: In the UK and Europe, the years 1987 until 1989 were marked by a large-scale revival of many characteristics of the hippie movement.

revivals.subject: hipster vintage
revivals.quote: Hipster fashion of the 2000s and 2010s prefigured many of the aesthetics of cottagecore.

revivals.subject: homburg
revivals.quote: The fedora and the homburg—revived when President Eisenhower wore one to his inauguration in 1952 rather than the customary top hat—were the most fashionable styles, with brims generally narrower than in previous decades.

revivals.subject: clear frame glasses
revivals.quote: 1960s fashion inspired glasses with clear and transparent frames had become common in this decade as well.

revivals.subject: dogtooth check jacket
revivals.quote: Popular shirts, coats, and dresses from this time included puffer jackets made from up-cycled deadstock fabric, sweatshirts, high waisted pants, tucked-in sweaters, camisoles and crop tops, low-rise miniskirts, brocade topcoats, midriff-baring tops, ribbed turtlenecks, garish Ed Hardy style T-shirts with rhinestones, off-the-shoulder knitted tops, science fiction-inspired metallic jackets, loose-fitting shift dresses or blouses, pantywaist tops sometimes with cap sleeves, cashmere cardigans, and oversized 1980s-inspired dog's tooth check jackets popularized by Kaia Gerber and Miley Cyrus.

revivals.subject: corseted silhouette
revivals.quote: Marcel Rochas introduced his celebrated "Femme" fragrance in 1945 and revived a corseted silhouette, becoming particularly celebrated for eveningwear executed in black Chantilly lace.

revivals.subject: indie sleaze
revivals.quote: The indie sleaze revival of the 2020s draws inspiration from the American Apparel-aesthetic and the late 2000s indie electronic and electroclash scenes.

revivals.subject: ivy league
revivals.quote: Known as Squares, Socs, and Jocks, this subculture underwent a revival in the 1980s as the preppy look.

revivals.subject: ivy league
revivals.quote: During the early 2010s, American preppy guys moved away from the hip-hop influenced fashions of the 2000s and begun to dress in a more classic 1950s Ivy League style with sweaters, Sperry Top-Sider boat shoes, Aran sweaters, cardigans, Oxford shirts, Cricket pullovers, wingtips, stripy polo shirts with layered shirts underneath in cooler weather, hats like the fedora, khaki or pastel colored Vineyard Vines, Nantucket Reds, white or bright pastel color socks worn with sneakers and Sperry Top-Sider boat shoes, white casual sneakers especially from Vans and Sperrys brands, colored jeans, white Nike Elite crew socks, baseball jackets, and khaki shorts.

revivals.subject: kinderwhore
revivals.quote: Fairy grunge can be seen as a natural extension of the kinderwhore style — which has deep roots in grunge, but with a more ethereal note.

revivals.subject: hippie maxi dress
revivals.quote: Typical clothing includes prairie dresses, blue gingham mini-dresses, white gypsy tops with multicolored Mexican-inspired floral embroidery, and hippie-style maxi dresses inspired by those worn during the late 1960s.

revivals.subject: 1980s military details
revivals.quote: From 2005 through the end of the decade, military-inspired clothing became a popular trend for both mean and women in Britain.

revivals.subject: suede miniskirt
revivals.quote: This style was also popular in the early 2000s.

revivals.subject: mod
revivals.quote: Seeking a return to the music and fashions of the mid and late 1960s, members of these British subcultures wore Ben Sherman shirts, slim fit pants, tank top sweaters, turtleneck sweaters, vintage striped boating blazers, basket weave brogue shoes, black leather driving gloves, pork pie hats, Irish walking hats, and loose fitting Oxford bags for dancing.

revivals.subject: mod
revivals.quote: The release of the cult film Quadrophenia in 1978 sparked a large scale Mod revival among a younger generation of Lambretta and Vespa scooter enthusiasts influenced by punk rock and new wave music.

revivals.subject: mod
revivals.quote: It was followed by a similar mod revival in North America in the early 1980s, particularly in southern California.

revivals.subject: mod
revivals.quote: The 1990s Britpop scene featured noticeable mod influences on bands such as Oasis, Blur, Ocean Colour Scene and the Bluetones.

revivals.subject: mod
revivals.quote: During the middle of the 2000s, retro fashion influenced by British indie pop, garage rock revivalist bands, and 1960s mod culture gained popularity.

revivals.subject: 1960s mod
revivals.quote: Members of the UK indie subculture mixed thrift store clothing from the mid-2000s to early 2010s with vintage items and new clothes made in retro 1960s styles by brands like Madcap England.

revivals.subject: beatles haircut
revivals.quote: British hipsters frequently left their undercut unstyled in imitation of 1990s Britpop and early Beatles haircuts.

revivals.subject: mod haircut
revivals.quote: By 2025 the mod haircut and large sideburns had made a comeback among younger guys in London, Northern England, the Eastern US, and parts of Australia due to a resurgence of interest in 2000s indie rock and 1990s Britpop groups like Oasis.

revivals.subject: narrow lapels
revivals.quote: Three-piece suits began their decline in the early 1980s and lapels on suits became very narrow, akin to that of the early 1960s.

revivals.subject: nehru jacket
revivals.quote: Crolla's giant cabbage rose prints, modeled after old chintz drapery fabric and needlework, seemed ubiquitous in 1984 and '85, initially shown by the designer on sixties-revival Nehru jackets and avant-garde UK street silhouettes like oversized sweaters and ankle-length tube skirts but soon picked up by Jean-Paul Gaultier in Paris and, before long, mass-marketed everywhere, especially popular in drop-waist, bertha-collared, puff-sleeved dresses to the lower calf put out by companies like Laura Ashley and worn with matching large hair bows on the back of the head.

revivals.subject: edwardian styles
revivals.quote: By the end of the decade, young men in Britain were looking instead toward Savile Row's highly tailored "Edwardian" styles.

revivals.subject: edwardian formality
revivals.quote: In Britain, Savile Row tailors revived a near-Edwardian formality: slightly fitted dark suits, some with striped trousers, were worn with Chesterfield coats, bowler hats, and well-polished black Oxford shoes.

revivals.subject: edwardian piping
revivals.quote: Some European single-breasted suits featured contrasting piping inspired by Edwardian fashion.

revivals.subject: neo-medieval
revivals.quote: Sometimes known as bardcore or castle-core, this trend combined feminism with hedonistic luxury fabrics like velvet, lace, jacquard, silk, leather, fur, and brocade.

revivals.subject: 1980s neon streetwear
revivals.quote: Throughout the decade, retro revivals persisted, including 1980s-style neon streetwear and tailored or fit-and-flare mid-century silhouettes that reflected the growing interest in vintage fashion.

revivals.subject: new romantic
revivals.quote: In the mid-1990s, the New Romantic era was the subject of nostalgia-oriented club nights — such as the Human League-inspired "Don't You Want Me", and "Planet Earth", a Duran Duran-themed night club whose promoter told The Sunday Times, "It's more of a celebration than a revival".

revivals.subject: seinfeld
revivals.quote: The characters featured on the sitcom Seinfeld (1989–1998) are frequently cited as exemplifying the aesthetics and ethos of normcore fashion.

revivals.subject: peplum
revivals.quote: Often paired with pencil skirts or skinny jeans, the peplum echoed mid-20th century tailoring.

revivals.subject: 1950s pin-up
revivals.quote: Visually, it was a mesh of various styles, ranging from 1930s Hollywood glamour, through 1950s pin-up sex appeal, pre-war cabaret theatrics, Victorian literary and symbolist styles, science fiction, to ancient and occult mysticism and mythology; manifesting itself in outrageous clothes, makeup, hairstyles, and platform-soled boots.

revivals.subject: pin-up
revivals.quote: Later in the decade, it was popular for women to dress like 1950s pin-up girls in polkadot dresses, pencil skirts, sheath dresses, capri pants, platform heels, 1940s style sandals, retro lingerie like garter belts, stockings, babydolls, petticoats, slips, and corsets, and (real or fake) old school tattoos.

revivals.subject: pinstripes
revivals.quote: Men's business attire saw a return of pinstripes for the first time since the 1970s.

revivals.subject: pointed collar
revivals.quote: Shirts with large and pointed collars became trendy again.

revivals.subject: pop punk
revivals.quote: In the early 2020s, alternative fashion drew on past subcultures like emo, pop punk, goth, and scene, as well as Japanese street style and emerging genres like hyperpop, nu metal, shoegaze, and rage music.

revivals.subject: power suit
revivals.quote: In the United States, the power suit also returned to popularity.

revivals.subject: 1980s power dressing
revivals.quote: Fitted blazers, often in bright colors such as teal or coral, were similarly popular, reflecting influences from 1980s power dressing.

revivals.subject: psychedelic
revivals.quote: The spring of 2021 saw a revival of psychedelic mid-to-late 1960s fashion worldwide.

revivals.subject: hardcore punk
revivals.quote: Hardcore punk fashion, which began in the 1970s, was very popular in the 1990s, especially among the skater subculture.

revivals.subject: scene
revivals.quote: In the early 2020s, alternative fashion drew on past subcultures like emo, pop punk, goth, and scene, as well as Japanese street style and emerging genres like hyperpop, nu metal, shoegaze, and rage music.

revivals.subject: scrunchie
revivals.quote: Many girls wore headbands, headwraps and 80s inspired scrunchies with either a side ponytail or french braid falling over one shoulder.

revivals.subject: shoulder pads
revivals.quote: Since the clothes were less comfortable and more restrictive than the clothes of the '70s and resembled too much the man-focused styles of the 1940s and '50s, this shoulder-padded look was initially a hard sell to the public, though women didn't demonstrate against big shoulder pads as they had against the midiskirt in 1970; they simply refused to buy the look.

revivals.subject: side-swept bangs
revivals.quote: By the late 00's, it became unfashionable to center-part one's hair, and the side-swept Bangs of the 1980s made a comeback.

revivals.subject: skinhead
revivals.quote: Most of these revivalist skinheads reacted to the commercialism of punk by adopting a look that was in line with the original 1969 skinhead style.

revivals.subject: skinhead
revivals.quote: The movement reached a peak at the end of the 1960s, experienced a revival in the 1980s, and, since then, has endured in multiple contexts worldwide.

revivals.subject: two-button suit
revivals.quote: The three-buttoned jackets common in the 1990s were increasingly replaced by two-buttoned suits influenced by 1950s designs.

revivals.subject: mad men suit
revivals.quote: This contrasted to Britain, Italy, Europe, and parts of the US, where more formal Mad Men-inspired business clothing such as slim-fitting grey two piece suits had made a comeback in the workplace during the early 2010s.

revivals.subject: soft grunge
revivals.quote: Associated with the indie sleaze and emerging soft grunge aesthetic, these designs drew loosely from punk, goth, and 1990s grunge styles but were increasingly detached from subcultural roots.

revivals.subject: soft grunge
revivals.quote: Around 2022, the soft grunge fashion style of the early to mid–2010s began to experience a resurgence in popularity due to videos uploaded on TikTok.

revivals.subject: costume jewelry
revivals.quote: These chunky pieces echoed 1980s power dressing and 1950s costume jewelry, contributing to the overall look of retro maximalism.

revivals.subject: pointed toes and spiked heels
revivals.quote: Meanwhile, women's fashion and business shoes revisited the pointed toes and spiked heels that were popular in the 1950s and early 1960s.

revivals.subject: nylon stockings
revivals.quote: The return of nylon stockings after their wartime absence was greeted with enormous relief; innovations included seamless stockings and new textures.

revivals.subject: streetwear
revivals.quote: By the late 1990s, the grunge look became unfashionable, and there was a revival of interest in streetwear clothing, with name brand designers such as Calvin Klein and Ralph Lauren making a comeback.

revivals.subject: 2000s streetwear
revivals.quote: It drew inspiration from 2000s fashion, blending casual, functional pieces with luxury and expressive details.

revivals.subject: 1960s british pop
revivals.quote: Britpop bands show elements from the British pop music of the 1960s, glam rock and punk rock of the 1970s, and indie pop of the 1980s in their music, attitude, and clothing.

revivals.subject: british invasion
revivals.quote: Critics have compared the early 2020s indie rock revival, with its 1960s- and Noughties-inspired outfits, to the original British Invasion.

revivals.subject: old school tattoos
revivals.quote: However, these made a comeback in 2008 at the same time Ed Hardy accessories and the pin-up girl look were becoming popular.

revivals.subject: old school tattoos
revivals.quote: Traditional, Old school tattoo, and retro revival or pinup girl style tattoos were especially prominent.

revivals.subject: tea gown
revivals.quote: Loungewear and negligees became more prominent in the fashion media, with the old-fashioned term "tea gown" making a return.

revivals.subject: teddy boys
revivals.quote: Concurrently, a resurgence of interest in Teddy Boy fashions was promoted by Vivienne Westwood and Malcolm McLaren through their shop Let it Rock, on London's King's Road.

revivals.subject: teddy boys
revivals.quote: In the late 1980s, there was a move by a number of Teddy Boys to revive the 1950s Teddy Boy style.

revivals.subject: teddy boys
revivals.quote: In the early 1990s, a group of Teddy Boy revivalists in the Tottenham area of north London formed "The Edwardian Drape Society" (T.E.D.S.).

revivals.subject: teddy boy collar
revivals.quote: Desirable items included suede cowboy boots and winklepickers, stone grey suits with Teddy Boy inspired velvet shawl collars, retro black and red sneakers, Chelsea boots with contrasting red and blue elastic, striped dress shirts, sailor T shirts with vertical navy blue stripes, tropical print shirts, navy and red track jackets, two button cream trenchcoats, corduroy sportcoats worn with turtle neck sweaters, double breasted navy blue or herringbone tweed overcoats with shawl collars, six button polo shirts, natural suede chukka boots, sunflower print button-down shirts, white T-shirts with orange and blue color blocks, turquoise dip dye swimshorts, military chic parkas, wool overcoats, red Superdry parkas with fur hoods, navy blue straw trilby hats, short sleeved cardigans, red Doc Martens, houndstooth or Prince of Wales check sportcoats, pants with a contrasting red stripe, lightweight nautical inspired navy peacoats, embroidered silk souvenir jackets featuring birds, skulls, dragons or tigers, bomber jackets with orange linings, Converse modern sneakers in silver, red, royal blue, or green, muted Aloha shirts worn over plain T-shirts, brown flying jackets, corduroy pants, beige anoraks, pale denim slim-fit jeans and chinos, checked button down shirts in pink, blue, orange, red, and white with oversized Cuban collars, cropped black high waisted pants, Henley shirts, grey T-shirts, preppy striped polo shirts with wider collars, double strap combat boots, claret, teal, electric blue, or navy blue velvet tuxedo jackets, and psychedelic floral print shirts frequently worn tucked into the pants.

revivals.subject: black or white tights
revivals.quote: Trouser suits began to replace skirts, black or white tights and nude pantyhose made a comeback.

revivals.subject: tramp stamp
revivals.quote: From 2021 onwards, new tattoo styles emerged among younger trendsetters.

revivals.subject: union jack
revivals.quote: The Union Jack became a prominent symbol of the movement (as it had a generation earlier with mod bands such as the Who) and its use as a symbol of pride and nationalism contrasted deeply with the controversy that erupted just a few years before when former Smiths singer Morrissey performed draped in it.

revivals.subject: miami vice suit
revivals.quote: Miami Vice-inspired suits were also trendy.

revivals.subject: waistcoat
revivals.quote: As part of the general 1980s revival, the waistcoat made a comeback as part of the three piece suit in Europe and the US.

revivals.subject: wedge sneakers
revivals.quote: Indie sleaze is making a comeback in the fashion industry among Gen Z. Isabel Marant wedge sneakers are making a comeback.

revivals.subject: embroidered western shirt
revivals.quote: The nudie suits and elaborately embroidered Rockmount shirts of the 1940s were updated with psychedelic hippie inspired motifs including naked women, cannabis leaves, sugar skulls, flames, Native American patterns, and brightly colored flowers like the rose or opium poppy.

revivals.subject: western shirt
revivals.quote: Other trends include printed shirts, zip-up cardigans, western shirts marketed to capitalise on the nostalgia for 1950s fashion, Birkenstocks, mood rings, and raincoats.

revivals.subject: western shirt
revivals.quote: Fitted Western-style shirts inspired by 1970s fashion, including designs with pearl snaps, gained attention through musicians such as the White Stripes.

revivals.subject: pearl snap western shirt
revivals.quote: Western shirts with pearl snaps returned to fashion, often made of denim, black gabardine, or bright madras plaid.

revivals.subject: western wear
revivals.quote: From the late 70s until the mid 80s, Western clothing made a comeback in America due to a resurgence of interest in country music, line dancing, western films, heartland rock, contemporary movies like Urban Cowboy, television series like Dallas, sports like cowboy action shooting, and the fashions and culture of the 1950s.

revivals.subject: 1940s-width lapels
revivals.quote: Lapels and ties for these new jacket styles were initially mostly narrow, said to help emphasize the increased shoulder width, but the most influential menswear designer of the time, Giorgio Armani, relatively quickly widened his lapels and ties – not as wide as in the early seventies, though, more like the 1940s.

revivals.subject: y2k
revivals.quote: Influenced by an early 2000s "Y2K" revival and the fashion experiments of celebrities such as Beyoncé, Nicki Minaj, and Emily Ratajkowski, club-wear incorporated bodysuits, with some celebrities choosing ones made from vintage Adidas and Chicago Bulls jerseys, vinyl outerwear, and sheer or iridescent fabrics.

revivals.subject: y2k
revivals.quote: The early 2020s trend cycle seemed to contradict itself, with microtrends like the Y2K revival and early 2010s nostalgia emerging alongside the millennial backlash.

revivals.subject: pachuco
revivals.quote: Pachuco style Zoot suits, fedoras and panama hats made a comeback, together with more typical casual rockabilly fashions for everyday wear such as slim jeans, black leather jackets, bowling shirts, brightly colored blouses and flouncy skirts for girls, polka dot dresses with petticoats, and flowers worn in the hair.
